questions.q: What does Seneca say makes humans truly unique among all creatures?
a: Our capacity for rational thought
Our ability to feel strong emotions
Our desire to form friendships
Our awareness that we will die
questions.why: The first lesson says Seneca believed rational thought is what sets us apart, so we should exercise it as fully as possible.

questions.q: What is the Stoic goal of gaining wisdom?
a: To live simply and in harmony with nature
To win fame and lasting fortune
To remove every emotion from daily life
To master public speaking and debate
questions.why: The summary says wisdom lets us live more in tune with nature, simply and without chasing excessive pleasure or status.

questions.q: What image does Seneca use for a healthy mind?
a: A well-loaded ship with everything secured
A clear mirror that reflects other people
A quiet garden hidden behind a wall
A strong fortress built on a hill
questions.why: In one letter he compares a healthy mind to a well-loaded ship whose cargo is fastened, so the view stays clear in rough seas.

questions.q: According to the Stoic view, what is the only thing you really control?
a: Your own thoughts
Other people's opinions
The events that happen to you
The length of your life
questions.why: The second lesson says our thoughts are the only thing we truly control, which is why Stoicism trains perception, action and will.

questions.q: Why do Stoics make such good friends, according to the summary?
a: They are self-sufficient and trust the few they choose
They need friends to fill an inner emptiness
They gather many acquaintances for practical use
They avoid close bonds to protect their independence
questions.why: The third lesson says Stoics befriend from abundance rather than need, select carefully and then trust fully.
